what: Li Auto makes electric SUVs in China. Most of its vehicles are extended-range models: they run on electricity but carry a small petrol engine that recharges the battery, which removes range anxiety.
customers: Chinese families buying premium SUVs, sold through its own showrooms.
money: L-series extended-range SUVs and the MEGA and i-series battery electric models
moat: The extended-range format gave it a category of its own in China for several years, with a family-focused interior design that buyers chose specifically.
risks: A net loss of $692M and $2.3B of negative free cash flow as sales fell
Revenue dropped from $19.8B to $16.1B as Chinese competitors matched the format
Chinese electric vehicle price competition is severe and shows no sign of easing
opportunities: $9.0B of cash against $2.5B of debt, enough to fund several years of losses
Analysts see about 33% upside, with 23 covering the stock
The battery electric i-series extends the range of products beyond the format rivals have copied
watch: Monthly deliveries and the gross margin per vehicle.
